prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting failed building fire-safety checks

1. Start with the inspection records.
2.
completion:
Identify the building’s main criterion for inspection – this determines the pattern for the Fire Safety Risk Assessment.

$\Rightarrow$ A guide for helping to complete a Fire Safety Risk Assessment for a building – here.

3. Prepare for a visit. Create an order of checks that can be consecutively reviewed. Take all documents that may be required for the visit and checks. Create a general checklist. Examine previous inspections or audits of fire-safety if available.

$\Rightarrow$ Visit are an opportunity to observe, note down and to take photos.4. Research the Fire Safety Act 2021.

## © A crucial point...

A record of past fire safety visits will be of great importance if a building is devastated by a fire in the future. Invest time in documenting any outstanding or not-negligible findings, be it in historic or modern buildings.

5. The dutyholder must have a record of all failed fire
